description: Approved Architecture Decision Records. An ADR is either an exception record (lists standards in authorises_exception_to) or a plain decision record (omits authorises_exception_to). Exception ADRs authorise a design choice that would otherwise violate a standard marked adr_overridable: true; cite the ADR ID inline where the authorised pattern appears and in any pr-reviewer finding to downgrade the severity to Informational. Decision-only ADRs record context, rationale, and consequences for a significant architectural choice that contradicts no standard; they are available as context but do not downgrade any finding.

adrs.title: Agent scratch is a place, not a procedure
adrs.rationale: Agents were told to reproduce a bash heredoc to stage working files. They paraphrased it, the paraphrase failed the tool allowlist, and they silently fell back to writing in the repository root. Naming an absolute directory and letting agents use their ordinary file tool removes the recipe, and with it the class of failure.
adrs.context: Between 2026-06-15 and 2026-08-21 three independent protections kept agent working files out of the repository: each agent ran an explicit rm -f cleanup, .gitignore matched the fixed filenames those agents used, and the names were predictable enough for that to work. Commit 01c1037 (2026-08-20) introduced an orchestrator-managed scratch directory and removed the per-agent cleanup, on the premise that files would now land in $AI_AGILE_SCRATCH. The premise did not hold: the PreToolUse scope hook added two days earlier (e00c9ed) denies the documented heredoc idiom as soon as an agent prefixes it with a variable assignment, which agents routinely do. With the safe route blocked, agents fell back to the Write tool, which has no path restriction, so relative filenames resolved to the repository root. The filename change also silently stopped .gitignore matching, and PR #371 then removed those rules as dead. Three agents in three phases were observed leaking (prd-writer, pr-reviewer, issue-classifier) across a single issue's pipeline run.
adrs.decision: Scratch is defined as a location, not as a procedure an agent must reproduce. AGENTS.md names $AI_AGILE_SCRATCH as an absolute path and instructs agents to create working files there with the Write tool, which every agent already holds and which requires no shell quoting. The bash heredoc example is removed, because reproducing it is what fails. The orchestrator continues to own the directory lifecycle through the declared agent_lifecycle scripts, and additionally sweeps the repository root after every agent invocation, removing files that were not present beforehand. This mirrors how Claude Code natively provides a scratchpad: an absolute path stated once, written to with ordinary file tools.
adrs.consequences: Agents no longer need cat, mkdir or rm grants to stage a file, and the leading-assignment trap disappears. Compliance no longer depends on an agent reproducing an idiom correctly: the root sweep is deterministic, runs for every agent rather than only git_ops.commit_after ones, and cannot be forgotten. The cost is that the sweep deletes files an agent wrote to the root, so an agent that legitimately needs to create a new root-level file must do so through a step that commits it; no current agent does. The ${AI_AGILE_SCRATCH:-/tmp} fallback is retained deliberately. Dropping it was considered and rejected: with the variable unset, "$AI_AGILE_SCRATCH/body.md" expands to "/body.md", a write to the filesystem root. The fallback resolves to a path that always exists, so an unset variable degrades to a shared /tmp rather than to /.
